                                        1    Introduction                                                          are required to make them operationally reliable in real-world use.
                                        This work does not argue that LLM-based systems are inherently             This has direct implications for enterprise-scale adoption, where
                                        ineffective. Rather, it examines the limits of autonomous operation        unstable repair loops can reduce the reliability of automated testing
                                        in a realistic enterprise UI environment and analyzes the recurring        workflows.
                                        failure modes that emerge under unconstrained autonomy.                    Contributions:
                                                                                                                                  Hyukjoo Lee


• We provide a quantitative empirical analysis of failure modes
  in LLM-driven autonomous test repair, based on 300 execution
  reports and 636 individual test-case executions collected from
  an anonymized enterprise-scale UI testing environment.
• We identify key limitations of High-autonomy repair loops—
  including non-converging repair behavior, hallucinated UI in-
  teractions, false-positive validation through assertion weaken-
  ing and test deletion, non-executable output generation, and
  environment-coupled recovery failures—and report their fre-
  quencies and co-occurrence patterns.
• We derive a controlled multi-agent workflow and associated
  design guidelines, validated against the observed failure dis-
  tribution, that define the operational constraints required for
  stable and reliable autonomous testing in enterprise-scale envi-
  ronments.

                                                                            The Coder agent generates interactions with UI elements that do not

3.4     Uncertainty Propagation

A key architectural property is tight inter-agent coupling: each            UI concepts with likely identifiers based on training patterns. The
agent’s output directly seeds the next. Errors and uncertainty there-       resulting code appears superficially plausible but fails at runtime—
fore accumulate across stages. An incorrect feature inferred during         or worse, silently interacts with the wrong element.
discovery propagates into an invalid scenario, which propagates                Across the 300-report corpus, we identified 6 distinct hallu-
into incorrect code, and ultimately into ineffective repair attempts.       cinated selectors and interaction APIs, including fabricated
The system behaves not as a collection of independent modules               page-object methods corresponding to navigation and filtering op-
but as a tightly coupled chain in which uncertainty compounds               erations that did not exist in the codebase, non-existent test-specific
forward.                                                                    DOM attributes, and incorrect label text in role-based selectors (e.g.,
                                                                            generating selectors based on inferred UI terminology that did not
                                                                            match the application’s actual labels). These hallucinated artifacts

intended behavior. We observed two distinct mechanisms by which
the agent achieved superficial convergence:                               5.5    Environment and Navigation Recovery

checks with trivially satisfied conditions to achieve a passing result.

illustrates the cost of implicit contracts: the system iterated 113      tical decision boundary: which parts of testing can be safely au-

                                                                         ary is essential for integrating autonomous testing into existing
                                                                         enterprise testing pipelines without compromising reliability. This
                                                                         enables practitioners to incrementally adopt autonomy rather than
                                                                         replacing existing workflows.
9    Controlled Autonomy Framework                                           The framework should be read not as a claim that autonomous
The five guidelines motivate a controlled autonomy framework.            repair becomes universally correct, but as a set of design constraints
Rather than choosing between full autonomy and full manual con-          required to operate such systems responsibly in production.
trol, the framework assigns LLMs to roles where their generative
strengths are beneficial, and applies deterministic constraints at
the points where LLM unreliability is structurally dangerous.
   These rules are derived from recurring failure patterns observed
across the 300-report evaluation corpus.
